title: Batch 2 · Winter markets to 2027
summary: Nine posts for December built on this season’s Instagram formats: winter-market moments, split screens, tiny-text POVs, rankings, saveable checklists and a year-end “Wrapped”. Set in a Calgary winter.

trends.name: Holiday and winter-market season
trends.why: Holiday sounds took over Reels right after Halloween. Shoppers plan gifts and outings on social media through December.
trends.used_in: weeks 4–5, set at winter markets with snow and “−20°” jokes

trends.name: Split-screen comparisons
trends.why: “Two ways” and before/after splits are among the formats trackers list this month.

trends.name: Tiny-text POV Reels
trends.why: Lo-fi, text-led, relatable Reels. One survey says half of users prefer unpolished Reels over highly produced ones.

trends.name: Rankings and listicles
trends.why: “Ranking X, worst to best” gets comments because people argue with the order.

trends.name: Saveable carousels
trends.why: Carousels lead on saves and shares. Since April 2026 Instagram favours original carousels and photos, not just Reels.

trends.name: “Send this to…” hooks
trends.why: Shares and DM sends now weigh heavily in reaching people who don’t follow you.

trends.name: Year-end “Wrapped” recaps
trends.why: Every December, brands copy the yearly-recap format. Bold stat cards, one number per slide.

trends.name: New Year resolution memes
trends.why: “Realistic edition” resolution lists come back every year between Christmas and January 1.

sources_note: Trend data comes from third-party trackers (Nov 2026) and changes weekly.
notes: The Dec 14 and Dec 16 posts show low-stock and sold-out features. Move them later if those aren’t live for vendors yet.
Wrapped figures are illustrative and labelled so on the images and in the caption.

weeks.title: Week 4 · Guests
weeks.sub: Winter market season: warm hands, no lines.

posts.caption:
Winter market, two ways. ❄️

Option 1: 25 minutes in line at −18°.
Option 2: scan the NO-Q code, order from the fire pit, and pick up when your number’s called.

We know which one your toes would pick. Look for NO-Q at your next winter market.

weeks.title: Week 5 · Vendors
weeks.sub: The holiday rush: stock, QR and live orders sorted.

posts.caption:
Holiday rush checklist for vendors ✅ Save this before your next winter market.

1. Set stock counts for your bestsellers
2. Turn on low-stock alerts, so guests see “Only 3 left”
3. Print your table QR and tape it to the counter
4. Keep live orders open, paid orders land there

Tag a vendor who’s doing markets this month.
alt: Lime cover: “Holiday rush checklist for vendors. 4 things to set up before your next winter market. Save this one,” with four empty checkboxes.
Step 1, set stock counts for your bestsellers: an inventory card with Jerk Chicken Plate 42, Beef Patty 60 and Sorrel 35, each with minus and plus buttons.
Step 2, turn on low-stock alerts: Jerk Chicken Plate marked “Low · 3”, Beef Patty marked “Sold out”, Sorrel at 18.
Step 3, print your table QR: an iPhone Duo showing the vendor storefront with its QR code.
Step 4, keep live orders open: an iPhone Duo showing the vendor’s live orders list.

posts.caption:
Stock that counts itself. 📉

Set a count for each item. Every NO-Q sale ticks it down, guests see “Only a few left” near the end, and at zero it flips to Sold out on every phone.

No more taking money for food you don’t have.
alt: Headline “Stock that counts itself.” A large lime 4 reads “left · Jerk Chicken Plate”, next to an iPhone showing the Jerk Chicken Plate with an “Only 4 left” badge.

posts.caption:
Send this to a vendor who’s still counting cash at −20° 🥶💵

With NO-Q, guests pay by card on their phones, orders show up on your screen and payouts go through Stripe. The gloves stay on.
